questions.q: According to the summary, what is the first step in explaining a complex idea to an audience?
a: Find a starting point you share with the audience
Make them curious with a striking fact or image
Explain each concept one at a time, in order
Use metaphors to tie new ideas to familiar ones
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists five steps, beginning with finding common ground with your audience.

questions.q: Why does showing vulnerability help a speaker persuade an audience?
a: It disarms listeners and makes them more open to your ideas
It proves the speaker has rehearsed the material thoroughly
It keeps the audience from noticing any small mistakes
It shows the speaker knows more than the people listening
questions.why: Lesson 1 says opening up gains trust, because people rarely let strangers protect their worldview.

questions.q: What does eye contact do for a speaker, according to the summary?
a: It earns trust, since listeners read truth and confidence in the eyes
It signals that the speaker is finishing the talk soon
It makes the room quieter so the speech can be heard
It helps the speaker remember the order of the slides
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that audiences can tell truth from lies and confidence from nerves by looking at your eyes.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend wearing for a public talk?
a: Something comfortable that still reflects who you are
All black, so the stage lighting flatters your face
The most formal outfit worn by anyone on the bill
Bright colors, so the audience remembers you later
questions.why: Lesson 3 reduces the dress code to one line: wear what makes you feel comfortable.

questions.q: If your talk will be recorded, which outfit does the summary advise avoiding?
a: All black or all white
Dark blue or dark grey
Bright red or bright green
Stripes or small checks
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that all black makes you look like a floating head and all white like a light bulb.
